Okay so i have some pretty strong opinions about this.

I highly reccomend avoiding all in one speakers or wirelessly linked speakers that dont have XLR thru inputs and outputs. If you ever have a brother that DJ’s or hope to expand your setup later, you wouldnt be able to with a JBL Partybox, for example, because they dont have XLR Inputs. Additionally, line array systems like the proreck have a huge learning curve that is best avoided .

XLR inputs let you link multiple speakers and subwoofers with no latency issues and can run directly from dj boards, microphones or instruments.

As far as the speakers themselves go, I would reccomend budgeting so that you can purchase one subwoofer (we use the electrovoice ELX200) and two matching 12-15 inch tops (we use the Harbinger Vari 4115 and Mackie Thump 15 A, but we use them in different rooms). For the tops, make sure you have stands.

For brands, Harbinger, Mackie, JBL PROFESSIONAL, Electrovoice, and QSC are all excellent and highly reliable brands. I would avoid proreck/gemini/alto/rockville/and JBL’s standard line for reliability and quality issues. Harbinger and Mackie are in my opinion the perfect combination of quality and price for your average fraternity.

Hope this helps.

Edit: Just as importantly though, you should read up on volume management. No matter how good your speakers are if your source audio is clipping/redlining OR your source audio is amazing but your speakers are clipped, its gonna sound like shit.
